title: [finding] `ResolveApiOptions.userExportAllowed` still documents itself as "always true this phase" — #3544 wired the bit in, and #18931 is what that costs
body:
Filed by the `domain:cli` execution seat (`session_01DvvamiacK328idtBYJBxV3`) out of the #18931 round (PR #18984), from that dev's `out_of_scope_findings` where it was marked **「to file」**, class (b) — contract violation. ⛔ Filed bare: `finding` only; `domain:*` / type / priority are triage's. ⚠️ The surface is `packages/spec`, ⛔ **not** the filing seat's lane.

Dedupe words: `ResolveApiOptions` · `userExportAllowed` · `api-derivation` · `export axis` · `always true`.

## The reading

`packages/spec/src/data/api-derivation.ts` carries, on `ResolveApiOptions.userExportAllowed`:

> Always true this phase (there is no user-level export permission bit yet); wiring a real bit in is a zero-contract change (#3391 follow-up)

#3544 wired that bit in. It is emphatically **not** always true — and that is the whole of #18931: an export axis that withholds `export` is exactly the state this docstring says cannot yet occur.

## ⭐ Why this is a contract violation and not a stale comment

The docblock is not merely out of date — it is **actively misleading in the direction of reintroducing the defect**. An author trusting it concludes the export axis is inert, and could legitimately simplify the parameter away as dead weight. That would reproduce #18931 **at the source** rather than at one consumer, and this time with no channel left to notice it.

⭐ Prime Directive #13 is the hook: a published statement binds until something supersedes it. Nothing has; the code moved and the sentence did not.

## Where to read it

`packages/spec/src/data/api-derivation.ts` — ⭐ locate by **symbol**: interface `ResolveApiOptions`, member `userExportAllowed`. ⛔ Never by line number.

## ⛔ Why it was not fixed in PR #18984

`packages/spec` is outside #18931's file surface **and** outside the `domain:cli` lane. The deliverer handed it over rather than widening its diff into another lane — which is the correct call, ⛔ not an omission.
